title: File tree service and REST controller
name: File tree API

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code separates the web, service and persistence layers? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A client asks to move folder A into a folder B that is a descendant of A. What happens?
choices: The move succeeds and the subtree becomes unreachable from the root.
assertNotDescendant walks up from B, finds A, and throws InvalidMoveException, which FileErrorHandler turns into a 409 response.
The database unique constraint on (owner_id, parent_id, name) rejects the update.
The service returns null and the controller responds with 404.

questions.prompt: Which layer decides that a quota failure becomes an HTTP 507 response, and why does that matter?
choices: FileService, because it throws QuotaExceededException with the status code embedded.
FileNodeRepository, because totalBytesOwnedBy computes the quota.
FileController.create, which catches the exception and builds the response.
FileErrorHandler: the service throws a domain exception with no HTTP knowledge, so it can be reused outside a web request.

questions.prompt: createFile publishes FileChanged inside a @Transactional method. If the transaction later fails to commit, what do you know about the listeners of that event?
choices: Nothing is guaranteed: a plain @EventListener runs synchronously when publishEvent is called, before the commit, so it may already have acted on data that is rolled back.
Listeners never run, because Spring defers every event to after commit.
Listeners run twice, once before and once after the commit.
Listeners run only if the commit succeeds, because publishEvent is bound to the transaction.
